newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal militants kill 11 in northeast India.
newsitem.headline: Tribal militants kill 11 in northeast India.

text.p: Separatist tribal militants on Saturday killed 11 people of a rival tribe in the northeastern Indian state of Manipur, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
PTI said the Naga separatists attacked a truck carrying members of the rival Kuki tribe and after killing them, set the vehicle on fire.
This was the first major strike by Naga militants since they ambushed 30 Kukis in December last year in the northeastern state of Nagaland, which borders Manipur.
The Nagas and the Kukis began fighting in mid-1992 for control of a highway which authorities say tribals use to transport drugs to neighbouring Burma.
Authorities say $1 billion worth of drugs is transported every year along the road, which was once firmly under the control of Kukis before the Nagas laid claim to it.
